item.title: Terrorism: FG secures 653 convictions, prosecutes 1,060 suspects
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Federal Government has secured a total of 653 convictions of persons arrested across the federation for their involvement in various acts of terrorism. The convicts, some of whom were found guilty of aiding insurgents or concealing information about their operations from security agencies, were among the 1,060 persons brought before the court in the third phase of the ongoing mass trial of terror suspects. Speaking to newsmen shortly after stepping out of the courtroom on Friday, the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who led the prosecution, disclosed that a total of 880 cases had been heard, out of which the court convicted 653, acquitted seven and discharged 27 of the defendants. He said the exercise would continue and the final figures would be announced after the conclusion of the trial. Describing the current phase of the mass trial as the largest since the FG commenced the special court sessions for the prosecution of terror suspects, the AGF attributed the success of the exercise to judicial cooperation, effective prosecution and inter-agency collaboration. He expressed appreciation to the judges handling the cases, particularly Justice Binta Nyako, who has been acting on behalf of the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho. The AGF also commended the prosecution team, the defence counsel and the security agencies for contributing to the smooth conduct of the proceedings. Among the agencies he acknowledged for their contributions were the Office of the National Security Adviser (NSA), the Department of State Services (DSS), the military, the police, correctional centres and the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria (LACoN). According to the AGF, collaboration among the institutions has been critical to advancing the prosecution of terrorism, terrorism financing and related offences in the country. On the representation of the defendants by lawyers from the LACoN, the AGF explained that the council was fulfilling its responsibility of providing legal assistance to eligible defendants. He clarified, however, that private legal practitioners were also representing some of the suspects. He said the defence lawyers were not only given the opportunity to interact with their clients before the court proceedings, but were also granted access to the detention facilities to enable them to prepare the defendants’ defence effectively. On the issue of deradicalisation of suspects recommended by the court, the AGF said the process remained an important component of the overall exercise. He maintained that rehabilitation and reintegration were necessary to complement the judicial process and reduce the risk of individuals returning to extremist activities. item.title: 2027: Adopt Rainbow Coalition model to avoid political violence, Wike urges govs

item.title: Tinubu condoles family of Nollywood veteran, Francis Duru‎‎
item.description: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu has expressed sorrow over the death of veteran Nollywood actor, Richard Francis Duru, extending his heartfelt condolences to his family, colleagues, fans and the Nigerian film industry. The veteran actor, Duru, passed away at 57. ‎ ‎The President, in a statement by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, described the loss of the respected actor as a painful moment for Nollywood and the nation’s creative community, which has benefited immensely from its pioneers’ dedication, talent, and contributions. ‎ ‎He acknowledged the important role veteran actors like Duru played in the growth and development of Nigeria’s film industry, particularly in shaping its artistic identity, nurturing emerging talent, and projecting Nigerian stories, culture, and values to audiences at home and abroad. ‎ ‎President Tinubu noted that the legacies of artists who devote their lives to entertaining, educating, and inspiring society endure long after their departure. ‎ ‎He affirmed that Duru’s contributions to Nollywood will remain part of the industry’s rich history and cultural heritage. ‎ ‎President Tinubu prayed for the peaceful repose of the departed actor’s soul and asked God to grant his family, friends, colleagues, and admirers the strength and fortitude to bear the irreparable loss. ‎ ‎He assured the Nigerian creative community that his administration recognises the invaluable contributions of the arts and entertainment industry to national development, cultural preservation, and the country’s global image. item.title: Bruno Fernandes’ home burgled during Man Utd’s 4-1 defeat to Como
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes’ home was burgled while the midfielder was in Italy with his team for their 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como on Wednesday, with police investigating the incident. According to ESPN, Fernandes’ family were not believed to have been at the property when the burglary occurred on Wednesday, October 21. Police attended the scene and Manchester United are supporting their captain. A statement from Cheshire Police, given to ESPN, said officers were called at about 8.30 pm to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley. “The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property,” the statement said. Officers found no trace of the suspects when they arrived but discovered that a burglary had taken place and a number of items had been stolen. “An investigation into the incident has been launched and enquiries are ongoing,” police added. Detective Inspector David Jarvis of Macclesfield Proactive CID said the investigation was at an early stage, adding that officers were working to identify those responsible. Police have appealed to anyone who was in the area at the time and may have witnessed suspicious activity to come forward. They also urged residents with relevant CCTV or dashcam footage to assist the investigation. The burglary came as United endured a difficult spell on the pitch, with their 4-1 defeat to Como extending their winless run to seven matches in all competitions. Fernandes publicly questioned the tactical approach of head coach Michael Carrick after the Champions League loss, saying the decision not to press opponents man-to-man and to leave space behind was a matter for the coaching staff. His comments followed criticism from United defender Lisandro Martínez the previous week, adding to scrutiny of the club’s leadership and performances. Despite the heavy defeat and questions over Carrick’s future, the United manager is expected to remain in charge for Sunday’s Premier League match against Bournemouth, ESPN reported. Fernandes, who was one of United’s standout performers last season, has struggled to reproduce the same form this campaign as the club faces growing pressure to improve its results. item.title: Tope Alabi threatens legal action over online defamation

The warning was contained in a public notice issued by her lawyers, Oakmount Legal Practitioners, and shared on the singer’s Instagram page on Friday, October 23, 2026. In the notice, the legal team said the singer, whose full name is Evangelist Patricia Temitope Alabi, had instructed them to take steps to protect her reputation against publications capable of causing damage to her personal, professional and spiritual standing. item.title: 2027: Wike debunks viral post backing Adamawa LP candidate, Abbo
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has debunked a social media post claiming he is backing Senator Ishaku Abbo, the Labour Party LP candidate in next year’s Adamawa State governorship election. Wike, who spoke through his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, described the report as fake. Olayinka said the minister has no relationship with the LP or any of its candidates in Adamawa State. The post in question quoted Wike as urging the people of Adamawa State to make informed and thoughtful decisions at the ballot, adding that, in his opinion, Abbo is best fit to lead the state. The minister, however, said he did not at any time endorse Abbo or any other LP candidate. He urged the people of Adamawa State to disregard the post, stressing that whoever he is supporting, he will say so with his own mouth. item.title: 2027: Tinubu’s aide claims CityBoy Movement has support across party lines
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Digital/New Media, O’tega Ogra, has claimed that the CityBoy Movement has been welcomed by a majority of Nigerian youths and has attracted members across party lines, including from opposition parties, ahead of the 2027 general election. Ogra, who is also Deputy Director-General of the CityBoy Movement, a group campaigning in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, made the claim on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday while responding to questions about the movement’s reach and acceptance among young Nigerians. When asked about areas where the movement had yet to gain acceptance, Ogra said he was open to discussing any such areas but maintained that the movement had received support from a majority of Nigerian youths. “I mean, if you show me one, I might be able to speak to that. But as far as I know, we have been welcomed by a majority of Nigerian youths,” he said. Ogra also claimed that the movement had members across the political divide, including people associated with major opposition parties. “We’re a movement that has members across the political space. We have members from the PDP. We have members from Alhaji Atiku’s own party. We have members that have come from Peter Obi’s own party. We have members who belong to Seyi Makinde’s government within our structure,” he said. Explaining what he believed was driving the movement’s appeal among young Nigerians, Ogra said youths were tired of political leaders who, in his view, made promises they failed to keep and diverted public funds for private interests. “Because at the end of the day, the Nigerian youths, we are done with people telling us lies. We are done with people promising one thing and putting government funds into their private enterprise,” he said. He further argued that young Nigerians were better equipped to scrutinise political leaders because of their access to information and fact-checking tools. “We’re done with people, you know, trying to play on our intelligence. We are smarter than whatever was in the 1990s or in the 2000s. We have access to news, we have access to information, we can fact check, we can revalidate, we have these things at our fingertips and one thing that we have chosen to do at the City Boy movement, our motto is inform, engage, empower,” Ogra added. item.title: Shun partisan politics, Aiyedatiwa tells Ondo corps members
item.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has charged members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) deployed to the state to avoid partisan politics in their host communities. Aiyedatiwa gave the charge at the closing ceremony and terminal parade of the 2026 Batch C Stream I orientation course held at Ikare-Akoko. Represented by the State Coordinator of the scheme, Mrs Kuburat Omowumi Bakare, the governor urged the corps members to be conscious of their responsibilities. “Remain mindful of the responsibilities that come with your position as corps members. Your actions will reflect not only on you but also on your families, your institutions and the NYSC,” he said. He appealed to employers and heads of establishments to receive corps members posted to them with cooperation and understanding. “Provide them with a conducive working environment, appropriate guidance and opportunities to contribute their knowledge and skills. Your mentorship can help them grow professionally and gain valuable experience that will serve them well beyond their service year,” Aiyedatiwa said. He also called on local government authorities, traditional rulers and community leaders to support corps members in their areas to aid their integration and effective execution of Community Development Service projects. “Your cooperation is essential to their successful integration into host communities and to the effective implementation of Community Development Service projects. By working together, we can ensure that the presence of corps members translates into tangible benefits for the people of Ondo State,” he added. The governor further urged the corps members to accept their postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for their host communities. “Approach your responsibilities with a strong sense of duty. Accept your postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for the people among whom you will live and work. Be willing to learn from your host communities, respect their customs and cultural values and conduct yourselves in ways that will earn their trust and confidence. “Your service year should be about more than fulfilling an obligation. It should be an opportunity to contribute meaningfully to society,” he said. Aiyedatiwa assured that his administration will continue to collaborate with security agencies and other stakeholders to ensure a safe environment for corps members throughout the service year. He cautioned them against compromising their personal security, advising them to remain vigilant, avoid late-night movements and unsafe gatherings, and shun unsolicited rides from strangers. “Be cautious when visiting unfamiliar or isolated places and promptly report suspicious activities or security concerns to the appropriate authorities. “Shun drug abuse, cybercrime, fraud and other unlawful activities that could jeopardise your future and bring disrepute to the scheme,” the governor added.

item.title: Atiku challenges Tinubu to name ministers, appointees involved in alleged bribery
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to identify those who allegedly received billions of naira in bribes from ministers to secure appointments, following the allegation by All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign spokesperson Alwan Hassan. Atiku made the demand in a post on his X handle on Friday, questioning who received the alleged payments and criticising the Tinubu administration over the rising cost of living and the funding of ministries. “Bola @officialABAT, your campaign spokesman has admitted that ministers paid billions in bribes to secure their appointments. You appointed them, so who received the money? Nigerians deserve names, not silence,” Atiku wrote. The former vice president also blamed the administration’s decisions for the cost-of-living crisis, alleging that the government’s handling of ministry funding had left Nigerians bearing the consequences. “Your government’s reckless decisions have driven the cost-of-living crisis. And when you withhold funds from ministries because you distrust your own ministers, Nigerians are left paying for a government that has abandoned them,” he added. Bola @officialABAT , your campaign spokesman has admitted that ministers paid billions in bribes to secure their appointments. You appointed them, so who received the money? Nigerians deserve names, not silence. Your government’s reckless decisions have driven the cost-of-living… pic.twitter.com/OlNYIfOCbf — Atiku Abubakar (@atiku) October 23, 2026 Hassan, a spokesperson for the APC Presidential Campaign Council, made the allegation during an interview on Arise News on Thursday while defending Tinubu’s record ahead of the 2027 general election. He alleged that some ministers pay billions of naira to secure appointments and then focus on recovering the money after assuming office. He also maintained that the practice was not limited to the APC administration but predated the party’s time in government. “A lot of ministers pay billions to be appointed, and the first thing they think of is how to recoup that money after being appointed,” Hassan said. “It is the truth about our country and not just APC ministers; it started before the APC,” he added. Hassan did not name any minister who allegedly paid for an appointment or identify the recipients of the purported payments in the reported interview. While defending Tinubu’s administration, the APC campaign spokesperson also cited government initiatives in the power sector and education, including funding for electricity meters and the renovation of primary schools and classrooms, as examples of the administration’s performance ahead of the 2027 election. item.title: Crude oil rises to $115 with stocks mixed on earnings, AI
item.description: Oil prices traded at five-month highs on Friday, with benchmark crude contract Brent North Sea rising above $115 a barrel, as the Middle East conflict raged on. Global markets were contending “with concerns around surging oil prices and the sustainability of AI spending”, noted AJ Bell head of financial analysis Danni Hewson. “Oil is at five-month highs amid speculation there may be renewed US-Israeli strikes after next month’s US midterm elections. “Escalating tensions in Ukraine and the prospect of increased energy demand as the northern hemisphere heads into the winter months are only adding to the upwards pressure on oil and gas prices,” Hewson added. Benchmark international oil contract Brent crude for December delivery rose as high as $115.45. Wall Street’s main indices slid at the start of trading, with the blue-chip Dow sinking one percent. “The ongoing agitation of the oil market has contributed to the lack of a buy-the-dip impulse” that has often helped Wall Street stocks avoid pulling lower this year. High oil prices also “keep inflation concerns and rate hike concerns on the front burner”, he added. Higher borrowing costs would make it more expensive for companies to borrow, which could pull the rug out from under breakneck development of AI that is being financed by debt and has underpinned the rise in equity markets this year. Stock markets mostly dropped in Europe following some poorly-received earnings from Gucci parent Kering and Swedish group Volvo Cars. Asian equity indices closed out the week mixed as technology firms managed to claw back some of the week’s hefty losses. Rising energy prices have influenced movements across stock markets in recent days along with developments in the AI sector. Facebook parent Meta and chip equipment maker Lam Research saw their share prices dive this week despite above-forecast earnings for the pair. “Strong results are no longer enough if the outlook fails to match an already demanding valuation,” noted Fawad Razaqzada, a markets analyst at traders FOREX.com. “Investors are becoming much less forgiving.” Non-AI companies have also seen their share prices slump this week. Kering shed more than 16 percent in Paris afternoon deals on Friday after the French luxury group published results that failed to reassure investors about a turnaround at its key Gucci brand. Volvo Cars meanwhile plunged more than 26 percent after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss. In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally. Aside from energy markets, AI and earnings next week, focus will fall firmly on interest-rate meetings for the US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank, as well as an update on US economic growth data. – Key figures at around 1330 GMT – Brent North Sea crude: UP 1.9 percent at $115.29 per barrel West Texas Intermediate: UP 2.3

item.title: Gunmen kill 7 at church in southern Jordan
item.description: Gunmen killed at least seven people and wounded 10 more in an attack on a church in southern Jordan on Friday, authorities said. Two assailants stormed the compound of a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hammoud in Karak governorate before opening fire, the public security directorate said in a statement. “Seven people died at least… while around 10 people were wounded, some of them critically,” the directorate said. The gunmen got out of a vehicle and opened fire during a funeral procession, it added, saying that a manhunt was underway for the perpetrators. Minister of Government Communications Mohammed Al-Momani said security forces were investigating the attack. An eyewitness told the kingdom’s state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka that a vehicle arrived carrying the gunmen, who fired continuously for five minutes before fleeing the scene. Between 150 and 200 people were in and around the church at the time, the witness said, adding that most of the victims were aged between 50 and 70. Karak is home to a significant Christian community in the Muslim-majority kingdom. AFP The post Gunmen kill 7 at church in southern Jordan appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Umahi accuses Obi of starting confrontation, faults his silence over supporters’ ‘Jesus’ remarks
item.description: Minister of Works David Umahi has accused former Anambra State governor Peter Obi of initiating their public disagreement, saying the Labour Party’s 2023 presidential candidate first confronted him at a construction site. In an interview with Arise News, Umahi said Obi had publicly criticised him while he was working at the site, describing the incident as unfair. “I did not criticise Peter Obi; he started the confrontation by coming to the construction site where I was working and publicly castigating me. I consider that very unfair,” Umahi said. The minister added that his comments about Obi were a response to what he described as a pattern of condemning others. “I only said that when you continually condemn others, you bring judgment upon yourself,” he said. Umahi also faulted Obi for allegedly failing to caution some of his supporters over comments he considered offensive to Christians. He cited a remark reportedly made by one of Obi’s supporters that even if Jesus contested an election, Obi would win, describing it as an affront to the Christian faith. “One of them reportedly said that even if Jesus contested in an election, Peter Obi would win. That is an affront to our faith, and I expected Peter Obi to speak out against such a statement,” he said. The minister’s comments followed his criticism of Obi’s presidential credentials, arguing that the former Anambra governor was not the best candidate the South-East could produce. “Peter Obi is not the best of our finest in South-East,” Umahi said. “He’s not the best; he can never be the best.” Umahi maintained that his position was not motivated by personal differences with Obi, but by his belief that the region had other qualified political figures who could pursue the presidency. The former Ebonyi State governor argued that anyone seeking to represent the South-East’s political interests at the national level should first consult governors and other influential leaders in the region. “You cannot play politics in South-East without consulting people like us,” he said. Umahi said building consensus among regional stakeholders was important for anyone seeking to advance a presidential ambition on behalf of the South-East. item.title: Man United goalie Onana rushed to hospital after car accident in Turkey
item.description: Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana was taken to hospital following a car accident in Turkey after Trabzonspor’s 2-0 victory over Hearts in the Conference League on Thursday. The Cameroon international was reportedly rear-ended by another vehicle, with images from the scene appearing to show debris from the collision. Onana was taken to hospital for medical checks but was later discharged after the results came back clear. Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan confirmed the incident while providing an update on the goalkeeper’s condition. “Andre Onana was involved in a road traffic accident earlier this evening. There are no problems with him, and we wish him a speedy recovery,” as reported by GOAL. Onana has made an impressive start to life at the Turkish club, where he is spending a second spell on loan from Manchester United. The 30-year-old started Thursday’s victory over Hearts, which followed Trabzonspor’s 4-2 win over Finnish side KuPS. The result also marked his fourth clean sheet in five games for the club. Trabzonspor have enjoyed a strong run of form in recent weeks, defeating Turkish heavyweights Besiktas and Galatasaray by an aggregate score of 6-0. The team will return to league action against Rizespor next Monday, giving Onana time to rest and recover before the fixture, depending on his condition following the accident. Onana joined Manchester United from Inter Milan in the summer of 2023 for £43.8 million but struggled to establish himself consistently during his time at Old Trafford. His position at the club came under pressure following the arrival of goalkeeper Senne Lammens, prompting his temporary move to Trabzonspor. During his previous spell at Manchester United, Onana made 42 appearances and kept six clean sheets. However, his return to Trabzonspor has offered signs of improvement, with the goalkeeper already approaching that clean-sheet tally as his side continues its positive start to the season. item.description: An 82-year-old Democratic state senator in Virginia, L. item.title: Casualties Feared As Multi-Storey Building Collapses In Nairobi
item.description: A multi-storey building collapsed mid-construction in the Kenyan capital on Friday, the Red Cross said, with reports from local media of casualties and looting at the site. Videos spreading online showed a dramatic crash and huge clouds of dust as the building — thought to have been around 18 storeys high — came down in a densely populated business and residential area of Eastleigh. AFP journalists at the scene saw the building had been reduced to a pile of rubble as a small number of search and rescue teams arrived on the scene. “There were some businesses in the basement and workers who were busy building,” said local resident Abdi Aziz, 25. “But as it was (the Friday prayer), a lot of them were at the mosque. I think few people died because no one was living there,” he told AFP. Asked if he could see obvious flaws in the construction process, he said, “Everyone rushes to build in this neighbourhood.” This aerial view shows personnel from the Kenya Defence Forces Disaster Response Battalion inspecting the rubble of a collapsed residential building that was still under construction in the Eastleigh neighbourhood of Nairobi on October 23, 2026. (Photo by TONY KARUMBA / AFP) | TONY KARUMBA / AFP Local media reported looting and possible casualties trapped beneath the rubble, with images showing large crowds gathered at the site immediately after the incident, which happened around lunchtime. AFP saw police use tear gas to disperse crowds gathering near the site. Rescue operations had yet to begin when AFP arrived, with the site hemmed in by high-rise buildings, complicating efforts. Nairobi is undergoing a rapid construction boom, with high-rise buildings appearing all over the city, particularly in Eastleigh which is known for its busy market areas and as a hub for the Somali community. There have been many concerns over safety. There were 86 building collapses between 2009 and 2019, killing an estimated 200 people, according to a report by the Kenya Institute for Public Policy Research and Analysis. An audit of almost 15,000 buildings by the National Building Inspectorate found that 4.8 percent were very dangerous, 72.3 percent were classified as unsafe, the report said. The number of buildings completed annually in Nairobi has risen from 20,025 in 2022 to 25,090 last year, according to its statistics bureau, as east Africa’s leading business hub sucks in people from rural areas and neighbouring countries. item.title: FG Designates Redeemer’s Health Village As TETFund Centre, Guarantees Scholarships For Robotic Surgery Academy
item.description: In a breakthrough for Nigeria’s healthcare sector, the Federal Government has adopted the newly inaugurated Redeemer’s Health Village (RHV) Robotic Surgery Academy as the nation’s 29th TETFund Centre of Excellence, guaranteeing full scholarship coverage for all enrolled trainees. Speaking at the official inauguration on Thursday, Minister of Education Dr. Tunji Alausa declared that the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) will fully fund the tuition fees of qualified medical professionals undergoing specialist training at the academy through its local scholarship scheme. ﻿ The strategic partnership — established alongside RoboMed Global, the National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria (NPMCN), and Redeemer’s University — establishes Nigeria’s pioneer institute for advanced robotic and telesurgical operations. ₦250bn Healthcare Injection Highlighting the government’s drive to curb brain drain and eliminate foreign medical tourism, Alausa disclosed that the Federal Government has injected over ₦250 billion into medical education across the last two years. “The same number of medical students admitted while I was in medical school is the same number we have maintained over the years, without sufficient consideration of our population growth,” the minister stated, confirming plans to expand annual medical programme enrolments to 20,000 within two years. According to RHV Chief Executive Officer Adedamola Dada, the academy aims to produce 400 certified specialists within two years across three main specialties: Urology, General Surgery, and Gynaecology.
